# The Markdown conformance suites

The fixtures behind `test/unit/tree_conformance_test.dart`, which measures
Niman's own reading of a note — the block tree, our inline parser and the
writer (`docs/dev/block-tree.md`) — against the specifications it follows:
`cmark-gfm`'s GFM, and CommonMark as a second count. These files are where
"conformant" stops being an assumption.

They first measured `package:markdown`, the parser before ours (645 / 652
CommonMark, 662 / 677 GFM, 2026-09-21); its gate and its allowlist went with
the package.

## What is here

| File | What it is | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `commonmark-0.31.2.json` | 652 examples in 26 sections | <https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/spec.json> |
| `gfm-0.29-gfm.json` | 677 examples in 31 sections | extracted from <https://github.github.com/gfm/> by `tool/extract_gfm_spec.py` |
| `cmark-gfm-extensions.txt` | 30 examples of `cmark-gfm`'s extensions — tables, strikethrough, autolinks, the tag filter, and footnotes, which no spec covers — in the spec's own `example` block format (`→` a tab, as in the spec) | <https://github.com/github/cmark-gfm/blob/master/test/extensions.txt>, downloaded 2026-10-06 |
| `tree_nonconforming.txt` | the examples our reading does not match, each with a bucket and a reason | curated by hand from a measurement |
| `html-normalize-corpus.json` | 375 HTML strings with cmark's own normalized answer | generated by `tool/gen_normalize_corpus.py` |

## Why GFM needs an extractor

CommonMark publishes its suite as JSON. **GitHub does not** — the `spec.json`
URL 404s — so the GFM examples have to come out of the published page. The
extractor also reproduces the two conventions the spec's own runner uses
(`cmark-gfm`'s `test/spec_tests.py:109-110`): the `→` glyph means a literal tab
in *both* the Markdown and the expected HTML, and the HTML side is
entity-encoded inside its `<pre><code>`.

Note that cmark-gfm's `test/spec.txt` is **not** the same suite: 672 examples,
and 12 of the published HTML's examples are missing from it while 7 of its own
are missing from the HTML. The published HTML is what "0.29-gfm" means to a
reader, so that is the one pinned here. Record the commit SHA if it is ever
re-extracted.

## Why the normalizer corpus exists

A conformance number is only meaningful relative to a normalizer: a lenient one
would report passes the reference would not. So `tool/html_normalize.dart` is a
port of cmark's `test/normalize.py`, and the corpus proves it — 375 cases,
byte-for-byte, covering both suites' expected HTML plus the reference's own
doctests and the branches the suites never reach (comments, declarations,
processing instructions, CDATA, valueless attributes, unknown entities, `<pre>`,
CRLF).

One case is knowingly not reproduced (CM 616 / GFM 639, a deliberately
malformed raw-HTML tag); it is pinned with its reason in
`test/unit/html_normalize_test.dart`, and it cannot change a verdict because
that example's expected HTML and the parser's output are the same string.

## Regenerating

```sh
# the GFM suite, from a saved copy of the published page
python3 tool/extract_gfm_spec.py gfm.html test/fixtures/spec/gfm-0.29-gfm.json

# the normalizer corpus (needs cmark's test/normalize.py on the path)
python3 tool/gen_normalize_corpus.py cm-0.31.2.json gfm-0.29-gfm.json \
    test/fixtures/spec/html-normalize-corpus.json

# the conformance report, by section, and the failures
dart run tool/tree_spec.dart
dart run tool/tree_spec.dart --failures
```

The examples are part of the specifications, not of Niman. The CommonMark spec
is published under CC BY-SA 4.0 (the spec text) with its reference
implementation under BSD-2-Clause; GitHub's GFM spec carries the same
inheritance from CommonMark. They are vendored here as test data, with their
source and version recorded above, and this note is the attribution. If Niman is
ever redistributed as a packaged product, this directory is the part to review.
